sections.title: Policy and access to the centre
sections.text: Le Haillan, in the western suburbs of Bordeaux, has a thin local rulebook. The town's 2025 map marks street parking as either unlimited or blue zone, with space counts per street such as 23, 55 and 61, but gives no time limits or prices, and the town's own parking page could not be opened, so the rules in force are unconfirmed [1]. The metropolitan low-emission zone has applied 24 hours a day inside the ring road since 1 January 2025 and bars only vehicles that cannot obtain a Crit'Air sticker; neither Cantinolle nor Rostand is among the 11 park-and-rides open to them, and the page does not say whether Le Haillan lies inside the zone [0]. A study from 2021 describes the Aéroparc business zone, partly in Le Haillan, with 3,000 establishments and 36,600 employees at the end of 2017, about 15% of the metropolis's private-sector jobs; it does not discuss parking [11].

sections.title: Parking developments
sections.text: Transport links are the story. Tram line D was extended by 5.5 km to a terminus called Eysines Cantinolle on 29 February 2020 [6]. Bus Express line G, 21 km from Saint-Aubin-de-Médoc to Bordeaux Saint-Jean and serving Le Haillan, was inaugurated on 1 June 2024, targeting 50,000 passengers a day, and the release says seven such lines are planned by 2027 [7]. The town's map shows a Mermoz park-and-ride planned for the first quarter of 2026 and an economic zone planned for 2027 [9], and a press article of 7 July 2026 reports that the Mermoz park-and-ride, at 57 avenue Pasteur, was inaugurated on 2 July with 366 spaces and 74 charging points; its headline rounds this to 400 and 75, it names no official source, and we found no official page [8]. Metropolis-wide, street charging costs 0.38 euro per kWh, with a surcharge of 4 euros an hour after four hours on slow sockets [10].

sections.title: Operators, positioning and utilisation
sections.text:
The two existing park-and-rides are Cantinolle (620 spaces, 15 disabled, 20 with charging) and Le Haillan Rostand (204 spaces, no charging), according to the metropolitan directory. Cantinolle costs a flat 3.50 euros for stays of 1 to 10 hours and Rostand 4.50 euros [2][4]. The directory points to the TBM site as the operator website for both and shows live counts of free spaces [3]. Cantinolle is one of 11 of the 28 park-and-rides selling short stays of 2 to 5 days at 12 to 25 euros, and Rostand is not [5].

Our data cover both sites for 27 days since 24 September 2026. Cantinolle averaged about 7% on weekdays and 5% at weekends and reached 20% at most, so it is nearly empty. Rostand, at the tram A terminus, averaged 14% on weekdays and 5% at weekends and reached 81% once, on a Saturday afternoon. Mermoz is not in our data.
